newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end 3.3 pct up, bank on budget hopes.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end 3.3 pct up, bank on budget hopes.

text.p: Bombay blue chips continued on Wednesday to claw back ground lost in the aftershock of the Congress party's move to oust Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition government, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange had surged 112.04 points, or 3.27 percent, at a provisional close of 3,539.05.
Growing confidence that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's widely acclaimed 1997/98 (April-March) budget will be salvaged out of the political mess shone through the gloom, dealers said.
"People expect the budget to be passed, positive statements by political parties have helped firm prices," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers.

The crippled 15-party government of Deve Gowda has to face a trust vote in parliament on April 11 after the Congress party on Sunday withdrew its crucial support, plunging the country into a political crisis and putting the budget in jeopardy.
But, parliament officials on Wednesday said major parties were efforting to rescue the budget from the political chaos.
Analysts said the market offered good investment values.

"I would recomend actually buying on the dip right now, because long term and medium term, India does offer very good earnings prospect," Dilip Rathore, senior economist at W.I. Carr told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday.
The Congress move chopped 302 points or over eight percent off the Bombay index on Monday, its fourth largest decline ever.

Hopes that sharp cuts in corporate and personal taxes proposed in the budget will not be tampered with helped shares climb two percent on Tuesday. A broad consensus among political parties on economic reforms spelt good news, analysts said.

"The crisis has given a message that there is a political consensus on the reforms and I think that would be the key to the further growth of investment into the country," Tushar Sarda, president and chief executive at Daewoo Securities told Reuters Financial Televison.
